description: What every platform's adapters must do on the real OS (plan §26, 'Platform adapters'). These aren't run by a shared runner: each platform's adapter tests implement every case.

command: for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do echo $i; sleep 0.5; done

from: rearchitecture-plan §9 RunningProcess.stop ((INT →) TERM → KILL, 5 s apart)

given.command: a child that ignores SIGINT (sh: trap '' INT)

expect.rule: Works without any main loop running (the watchdog has its own thread).
expect.windows: No signals: CTRL_BREAK to the tool's console (sent by a short-lived hidden PowerShell attached to it), then TerminateJobObject after 5 s or as soon as the tool has exited; a tool that exits on the break reports its own exit status, one the job ends reports -1; no signal.

from: docs/architecture.md#stopping-processes (makemkvcon ignores SIGINT: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 s)

given.command: a child that ignores SIGINT and SIGTERM

expect.windows: CTRL_BREAK, then TerminateJobObject after 5 s (as cancel-escalates).

from: docs/architecture.md#stopping-processes (still there 30 s after SIGKILL → abandoned)

given.command: a child stuck in the kernel

expect.note: Not reproducible in a test (a process stuck in the kernel); covered by reading the code.
expect.rule: An abandoned process may still be running and writing: whatever it was writing to (a staging folder, an image) must be quarantined, never reused or removed.

from: docs/architecture.md#stopping-processes (output read for at most 5 more seconds after exit)

expect.rule: The 5 s count from the last progress (see a-slow-reader-gets-everything).

from: the Linux launcher wrote the transcript without its lock, so a reader could write to the closed descriptor

given.then: right after wait returns, open 20 files and keep them open for 2 s

expect.rule: a line read after the process has ended (a child left behind kept the pipe open past 5 s) is dropped: it never reaches the transcript, which is closed, nor a file that reuses the transcript's descriptor; the transcript is written under the launcher's lock, so a reader still holding a line when the process ends can't write either

from: a tool writing binary with no line breaks grew the launcher's memory without limit

command: head -c 200000 /dev/zero | tr '\\0' a; echo; echo next

expect.rule: a line is cut after 65536 bytes and ends with ' [cut]'; the rest of it, up to the next line break, is dropped

given.command: 50000 numbered lines, then a marker file
given.then: read nothing for 3 s, then everything

expect.rule: at most 10000 lines, or 16 MiB of their text (UTF-8), wait to be read; then the reading waits, so the tool waits to write: nothing is lost, memory stays bounded (long lines for a reader that has stopped hold about 16 MiB, not 10000 x 64 KiB), and waiting for the reader isn't silence

given.command: 30000 numbered lines, then exit at once
given.then: read them slowly: about 15 s in all, so the backlog outlasts the 5 s after the exit

expect.rule: the launcher keeps reading for 5 s after an exit, and longer while lines wait for a reader that is still taking them: a slow reader loses nothing (lines still queued count as waiting, not only a launcher thread blocked for room); a child left holding the pipe still doesn't hold up the end (output-drained)

from: rearchitecture-plan §10.3 (posix_spawn + process group; Job Object; setpgid)

expect.rule: Signals go to the process group; once a stopped process has ended, what is left of its group is killed (a shell's background child ignores SIGINT). A process left running after a normal exit is left alone.
expect.windows: The Job Object: once a stopped tool has ended (or 5 s after CTRL_BREAK), TerminateJobObject ends every process left in it.

from: real-drive test, 2026-10-08: kill -9 of Bromelia --headless mid-rip left makemkvcon (it ignores SIGPIPE) reading the disc into the folder recovery had marked INCOMPLETE

command: sleep 60 & echo $! > child.pid; echo $$ > tool.pid; exec sleep 60
given.then: the engine process is killed (SIGKILL; TerminateProcess) while the tool runs, with no chance to stop it

expect.afterNormalExit: A tool that exited normally takes its watcher with it: what it left running is left alone, even when the engine is killed later (as process-group).
expect.macos: A watcher per process: /bin/sh in its own process group, its stdin the read end of a pipe whose write end only the engine holds (close-on-exec). When the engine ends, however it ends, the read returns and the watcher sends TERM to the tool's group, then KILL if the group is still there 5 s later (it stops watching as soon as the group is gone, so it never signals one used again). The watcher is killed and reaped when the tool ends, before the tool is reaped (so it never signals a reused group).
expect.linux: As macOS (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG isn't used: it fires when the thread that started the child ends).
expect.windows: The Job Object has KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE until the process has ended: the engine's handle closes with it and the job's processes end.

from: docs/architecture.md#per-drive-makemkv-settings (every line, headed by the command line, followed by the exit status)

expect.commandLine: ArgumentSplitter.quote of each word of the invocation (after the interpreter choice)

expect.rule: the tool runs anyway, and the run says its log is missing (RunningProcess.transcriptProblem), instead of carrying on without one in silence

expect.cancelled: cancelled true for StopReason cancelled and shutdown, never for policy (the engine's own decision: MakeMKV's space warning, a renumbered drive), stalled or timedOut
expect.stalled: stalled = the silence that stopped it

from: docs/architecture.md (lines split on \n, \r or \r\n; empty lines dropped)

expect.rule: The spec's environment is added to the engine's; stdin is empty (/dev/null); invalid UTF-8 is replaced.

cases: a working folder that doesn't exist
a script without the execute bit (macOS, Linux)

expect.windowsFullPaths: Windows' own programs by full path: a bare name is looked up in the engine's current folder before System32.

expect.rule: Only a bare drive letter is read as a device; a file on C: is read as that file.

expect.registry: HKCU\Software\MakeMKV gets the drive's values (other catalogue keys cleared) and the previous values back on the first output line, the exit or after 15 s; launches are serialised (MakemkvLaunch lease); a warning when the MakeMKV GUI runs
expect.snapshot: before any value changes, the user's values are written atomically to <data>\run\makemkv-registry.json (an owner-only folder: it can hold app_Key) and the file is removed once they are all back; a file left by a crash is put back by Recover() at startup or before the next launch, and a launch fails with makemkv.registryNotRestored while it can't be; a snapshot folder on a network share, or one where owner-only doesn't hold, fails the launch with fs.notPrivate before any value changes

expect.note: Replaces automation.lock (and its one-minute takeover): exactly one engine per user.

expect.folderSyncUnsupported: syncDirectory succeeds when the file system can't sync a folder at all (macOS, Linux: EINVAL or ENOTSUP; Windows: ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION or ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED, which the Windows SMB client answers for every folder): the rename has happened and nothing more can be asked of that file system. Any other failure is fs.failed.

from: rebuild-review-followups 2026-10-05 (owner: refuse network sharing of secrets)

given.keystoreFallbackFolder: on a network share (Windows: a UNC path or a drive GetDriveTypeW calls remote; macOS: a file system without MNT_LOCAL; Linux: NFS, SMB / CIFS, AFS, Coda, NCP or Ceph by statfs f_type)

expect.getAndSet: fs.notPrivate {path (the folder), reason}; nothing is written; remove still works
expect.ownerOnly: before each write the folder is made owner-only (macOS, Linux: chmod 0700 and the user's; Windows: OwnerOnly) and read back: if that didn't hold, fs.notPrivate
expect.registrySnapshot: the same rule for RegistrySwapIsolation's snapshot folder (settings-isolation-registry)
